schema_ddl:
CREATE TABLE ACTIVITY (
    PLAYER_ID INT,
    EVENT_DATE DATE,
    DEVICE_ID INT,
    GAMES_PLAYED INT,
    PRIMARY KEY (PLAYER_ID, EVENT_DATE),
    CHECK (GAMES_PLAYED >= 0)
);
q1: SELECT PLAYER_ID, DEVICE_ID FROM ACTIVITY WHERE (PLAYER_ID, EVENT_DATE) IN ( SELECT PLAYER_ID, MIN(EVENT_DATE) FROM ACTIVITY GROUP BY PLAYER_ID )
q2: SELECT A.PLAYER_ID, A.DEVICE_ID FROM ACTIVITY A JOIN (SELECT PLAYER_ID, MIN(EVENT_DATE) FIRST_LOGIN FROM ACTIVITY GROUP BY PLAYER_ID) T ON A.PLAYER_ID=T.PLAYER_ID AND A.EVENT_DATE = T.FIRST_LOGIN

q2_prompt_sql: SELECT A.PLAYER_ID, A.DEVICE_ID FROM ACTIVITY A JOIN (SELECT PLAYER_ID, MIN(EVENT_DATE) FIRST_LOGIN FROM ACTIVITY GROUP BY PLAYER_ID) T ON A.PLAYER_ID=T.PLAYER_ID AND A.EVENT_DATE = T.FIRST_LOGIN
counterexample: INSERT INTO ACTIVITY (PLAYER_ID, EVENT_DATE, DEVICE_ID, GAMES_PLAYED) VALUES (1, '2023-01-01', 100, 2); INSERT INTO ACTIVITY (PLAYER_ID, EVENT_DATE, DEVICE_ID, GAMES_PLAYED) VALUES (1, '2023-01-01', 101, 3); INSERT INTO ACTIVITY (PLAYER_ID, EVENT_DATE, DEVICE_ID, GAMES_PLAYED) VALUES (2, '2023-01-02', 200, 1);
explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not semantically equivalent. Q1 selects rows from ACTIVITY where the (PLAYER_ID, EVENT_DATE) pair matches the minimum EVENT_DATE for each PLAYER_ID. However, Q2 joins on both PLAYER_ID and EVENT_DATE, ensuring the row from ACTIVITY matches the exact row from the subquery that contains the minimum EVENT_DATE. In cases where multiple rows share the same minimum EVENT_DATE for a given PLAYER_ID, Q1 will return all those rows, while Q2 will return only one row per PLAYER_ID (the one matched by the join).
counterexample_dsp: A scenario where a player has multiple rows with the same minimum event date. Q1 will return all those rows, but Q2 will return only one.
